You are resolving an in-progress git merge in treams-rs (branch claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh). It merges commit 84ec1bc (condensed into 8251007) ("RB2": Rust core periodic work in crates/treams-core/src/{lattice.rs, geometry.rs, conversion.rs, channels.rs} — Bloch reduction, basis-choice independence of Ewald sums, hexagonal first_brillouin at every length scale, 3D convergence cap, batched Ewald tables, new proptests — plus some Python test trims where Rust now covers invariants) into the integration branch, which already contains the Python test-lane rewrites (PB0 foundation with tests/_support.py and mandatory category markers; PB1/PB2/PB3), bindings lanes PA1/PA2/PA3/PA4 (PA2 removed the test-only _native.lattice_sum/_native.lattice_derivatives bindings and routes lattice tests through the public diff.lattice_sum), S1 and RB1. Do not abort the merge.

Conflicts: tests/test_geometry_misc.py, tests/test_lattice.py, tests/test_lattice_sum_adjoints.py (check git status).

Rules:

  • Keep the test lanes' and PA2's current structure (public recorded paths, check_pullback/check_gradient, category markers, strict xfails that still apply) AND RB2's intent (its Python-side changes: removed duplicates now covered by named Rust proptests — keep those removals only if the named Rust test exists in crates/treams-core after the merge; new/changed Python assertions for its fixes, e.g. Bloch/basis independence, hexagonal Brillouin zones). Inspect each side with git log -p MERGE_HEAD --not HEAD -- <file> and git log -p HEAD --not MERGE_HEAD -- <file>.
  • RB2 may have fixed defects that the test lanes pinned as strict xfails (e.g. in test_lattice.py / test_geometry_misc.py or listed in docs/status.md's expected failures such as the lattice-sum tiny out-of-plane shift, or hexagonal first_brillouin). With xfail_strict=true a fixed one XPASS-fails: convert it to a plain test and remove the entry from docs/status.md. Leave xfails whose defect remains.
  • Every test must carry a registered category marker (tests/test_suite_contract.py guards it).

Verification (must all pass before committing): cd treams-rs && just build-ext (cold target, several minutes), cargo fmt --check --all, PYO3_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, PYO3_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python cargo test --locked -p treams-core, .venv/bin/ruff format --check . && .venv/bin/ruff check ., uv run --no-sync pyrefly check, uv run --no-sync python scripts/generate_agent_docs.py --check (regenerate and commit docs if it fails because of the merge), the full uv run --no-sync pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider, and PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python .venv/bin/python battery.py compare baseline.npz. The parity battery may show intended changes from RB2's correctness fixes in lattice cases; RB2's own report says its parity result was PASS, so any failure must be investigated and explained, not waved through. Commit the merge with message "Merge RB2: periodic lattice sums, diffraction geometry, periodic conversion and channels" plus a short body on the resolutions, ending with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud] Do NOT push; do not touch scratch: lanes or other branches. Report the resolutions, xfails converted, and verification results (test counts, parity summary).

I resolved and committed the RB2 merge in treams-rs as c50c7ab (condensed into 8251007) on claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh, with the requested message, resolution body and trailers. Every verification gate passed; I did not push or touch scratch: lanes.

How the three conflicts were resolved

  • tests/test_lattice.py
    • Removed test_bloch_scale_split_inversion_and_periodicity. This was the test lane's expanded version of the test RB2 deleted. Everything it checked (split, Bloch translation, scaling, inversion, reciprocal periodicity) is covered for every family, order and skewed lattice by the Rust tests properties::lattice::ewald_sums_are_lattice_covariant_and_point_symmetric and ewald_sums_depend_on_the_lattice_not_its_description. Both exist after the merge and pass.
    • Kept the lane's @pytest.mark.physics on test_tiny_out_of_plane_shift_is_continuous; it sat inside the conflict block and would otherwise have been lost.
    • test_all_continuous_lattice_derivatives: kept the lane's ad_contract/oracle_numerical markers and FAMILIES, and applied RB2's trim to (l, m) = (1, -1) and (3, 1). The dropped cases are covered by the Rust ewald_complete_derivative and ewald_derivative_identities, which exist and pass; I added a comment saying so.
    • Removed the now-unused degree_order import.
    • Changed RB2's docstring from "pyfunction derivatives" to "public-path derivatives", because PA2 removed that pyfunction.
  • tests/test_lattice_sum_adjoints.py: used the lane's naming (advect.numpy.real, ad.lattice_sum, advect.grad, degree) with RB2's split check: the full sum stays fixed at 0.9 while the parts are traced at 1.2.
  • tests/test_geometry_misc.py
    • Removed test_reciprocal_duality_and_scale, as RB2 did; geometry::reciprocal_duality exists and covers duality, involution and volumes.
    • Kept the lane's test_skew_diffraction_pairs_and_plane_basis (including the orders[0] == [0, 0] check and PlaneWavePorts). Its comment named a Rust test RB2 had removed, so it now points to geometry::diffraction_orders_are_complete_paired_and_unique.
    • Kept the lane's Brillouin 2D/3D, kz-branch and helicity-index tests, and added RB2's test_brillouin_accepts_hexagonal_lattices_at_any_pitch with a physics marker.
  • Auto-merged, reviewed: tests/test_lattice_decomposition.py (RB2's resplit check keeps the lane's physics marker), and docs/status.md and docs/upstream-findings.md. The new hexagonal-cell entry in docs/upstream-findings.md names tests that exist.

Xfails converted: none. RB2 fixed no pinned strict xfail. Both lattice-sum out-of-plane-shift cases still fail as expected (shared-with-upstream and diverges-from-upstream), so they stay, and so does their entry in docs/status.md. The hexagonal first_brillouin bug was never pinned as an xfail on the integration branch, so there was nothing to remove.

Verification

  • just build-ext: built successfully (debug extension).
  • cargo fmt --check --all: clean.
  • cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean.
  • cargo test --locked -p treams-core: 131 passed, 0 failed, including all the Rust tests named above.
  • ruff format --check and ruff check: clean.
  • pyrefly check: 0 errors.
  • generate_agent_docs.py --check: docs current, nothing regenerated.
  • Full pytest: 4320 passed, 36 skipped (matplotlib not installed, and inapplicable ufunc-layout cases), 27 xfailed, 0 xpassed.
  • Parity battery: PASS, 0 of 128 cases failing. The largest error was 2.33e-15 in lattice_sums_spherical_generic, well inside rtol 1e-10. This matches RB2's own PASS report, and there were no lattice-case changes to explain. The run happened before the commit, so it reports git a53998e (condensed into 8251007), but it used the freshly built merged extension.

Shared scratchpad: other agents use the same scratchpad directory. A lane-rc run overwrote my first pytest.log (its output showed lanes/rc and 1 xpassed). I discarded those logs and re-ran clippy, cargo test and pytest into a private subdirectory; the numbers above come from those re-runs.
